section.title: The ooSQLiteMutex Class
section.para: An ooSQLiteMutex object is an SQLite mutex: an object that the threads of a program use to take turns, so that only one of them at a time runs the code that it protects. A mutex is created with new, or obtained for a database connection with the dbMutex method of the ooSQLiteConnection class.
The oosqlMutex routines, such as oosqlMutexAlloc, do the same in the classic interface, with handles instead of objects.

section.title: Method Table
section.para: The following table provides links to the documentation of the methods and attributes of the ooSQLiteMutex class.

Tells whether the object has no SQLite mutex.

section.title: new (Class method)
section.para: Creates a new mutex object, which the threads of a program can use to take turns.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
type [optional]
The kind of mutex, one of the Mutex Type constants MUTEX_FAST or MUTEX_RECURSIVE. The default is MUTEX_FAST. A thread that holds a recursive mutex can enter it again; a thread that holds a fast mutex must not.
A new ooSQLiteMutex object. If SQLite could not allocate the mutex, which only happens when it was built without support for threads, the object is not usable: its isNull attribute is true.

What is said here applies to all the methods of a mutex. A mutex is held by one thread at a time: a thread enters it with enter, which waits while another thread holds it, or with try, which does not wait, and leaves it with leave. The thread that entered the mutex is the one that must leave it, once for each time it entered it. While a thread waits for a mutex, the other threads of the program keep running.

Entering a fast mutex again from the thread that holds it blocks the thread for ever, and leaving a mutex that the thread does not hold has undefined results. A mutex that has been freed with free can not be used: its methods raise an error.

The mutex is freed by free, or when the object is garbage collected. The dbMutex method of the ooSQLiteConnection class returns an ooSQLiteMutex object for the mutex of a connection, which belongs to SQLite. In Rexx code, the guarded methods and the GUARD instruction of ooRexx also make threads take turns; an SQLite mutex is mostly useful when other code that uses SQLite takes part, or to hold the mutex of a connection.
Raises a syntax error, 88.916, if type is not MUTEX_FAST or MUTEX_RECURSIVE. The other mutex types are the static mutexes that SQLite uses internally.
The functionality of the new method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_mutex_alloc API.
The oosqlMutexAlloc routine does the same in the classic interface.

In this example, three threads add 1000 to a shared counter each. Each addition reads the counter, lets the other threads run, and writes it back, so without the mutex the threads would overwrite each other's work and the total would be much lower:
mtx = .ooSQLiteMutex~new counter = .directory~new~~put(0, 'N') threads = .array~new do 3 threads~append(.message~new(.adder~new, 'add', 'I', mtx, counter)~~start) end do t over threads t~result -- waits until the thread ends end say counter['N'] mtx~free /* Output: 3000 */
::class adder ::method add use arg mtx, counter do 1000 mtx~enter n = counter['N'] call SysSleep 0 -- lets the other threads run counter['N'] = n + 1 mtx~leave end

section.title: &changed11;closed (Attribute)
section.para: Tells whether the mutex can no longer be used.

listitem.para: True if the mutex has been freed with free, if it could not be created, or if it is the mutex of a connection that has been closed; false while it can be used.
The Rexx programmer can not set the value of this attribute. It is set internally by the ooSQLite framework.

&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, a mutex returned by dbMutex was not closed when its connection was closed, and kept using the mutex that SQLite had freed. isNull tells whether there is a mutex at all.

This example shows the two attributes before and after the mutex is freed:
mtx = .ooSQLiteMutex~new(.ooSQLite~MUTEX_RECURSIVE) say 'closed:' mtx~closed 'isNull:' mtx~isNull mtx~free say 'closed:' mtx~closed 'isNull:' mtx~isNull /* Output: closed: 0 isNull: 0 closed: 1 isNull: 1 */

section.title: isNull (Attribute)
section.para: Tells whether the object has no SQLite mutex.

listitem.para: True if the object has no mutex: SQLite could not allocate it, it has been freed, or it was the mutex of a connection that has been closed. False otherwise.
The Rexx programmer can not set the value of this attribute. It is set internally by the ooSQLite framework.

A mutex returned by dbMutex is null when the connection is not in the serialized threading mode, because the connection has no mutex then. See the remarks of new for the rules that all the methods of a mutex follow.
See the example of closed.

section.title: &changed11;enter
section.para: Enters the mutex, waiting until no other thread holds it.

listitem.para: There are no arguments.
Returns OK.

A recursive mutex can be entered again by the thread that holds it; a fast mutex must not. Each enter must be matched by a leave from the same thread. See the remarks of new for the rules that all the methods of a mutex follow.
Raises an execution error, 98.900, with the message "The ooSQLite mutex is not valid, it has been closed" if the mutex has been freed, or if it is the mutex of a connection that has been closed.
The functionality of the enter method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_mutex_enter API.
The oosqlMutexEnter routine does the same in the classic interface.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, a freed mutex raised no error: the method did nothing.
See the example of new.
There are no arguments.
Returns OK.

The mutex must not be held by any thread. After free, the object can not be used any more: its methods raise an error, and its closed attribute is true. Freeing it again does nothing. A mutex is also freed when its object is garbage collected, so free is only needed to release it earlier.

For a mutex returned by dbMutex, which belongs to SQLite, free only closes the object: the mutex of the connection is not freed. See the remarks of new for the rules that all the methods of a mutex follow.
The functionality of the free method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_mutex_free API.
The oosqlMutexFree routine does the same in the classic interface.
See the examples of new and try.

section.title: &changed11;leave
section.para: Leaves the mutex, which the current thread holds.

listitem.para: There are no arguments.
Returns OK.

The mutex must have been entered by the same thread, with enter or with a successful try. A recursive mutex that was entered several times is released when it has been left as many times. See the remarks of new for the rules that all the methods of a mutex follow.
Raises an execution error, 98.900, with the message "The ooSQLite mutex is not valid, it has been closed" if the mutex has been freed, or if it is the mutex of a connection that has been closed.
The functionality of the leave method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_mutex_leave API.
The oosqlMutexLeave routine does the same in the classic interface.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, a freed mutex raised no error: the method did nothing.
See the examples of new and try.

section.title: &changed11;try
section.para: Tries to enter the mutex, without waiting if another thread holds it.

listitem.para: There are no arguments.
Returns OK if the mutex was entered: then it must be left with leave, as after enter. Returns BUSY if another thread holds the mutex.

A thread that holds a recursive mutex gets OK and enters it again. The result of trying a fast mutex that the same thread already holds is undefined. SQLite notes that on some systems this method always returns BUSY, so a program should not depend on it to work. See the remarks of new for the rules that all the methods of a mutex follow.
Raises an execution error, 98.900, with the message "The ooSQLite mutex is not valid, it has been closed" if the mutex has been freed, or if it is the mutex of a connection that has been closed.
The functionality of the try method is similar to that of the SQLite sqlite3_mutex_try API.
The oosqlMutexTry routine does the same in the classic interface.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, a freed mutex raised no error, and the method returned OK.

This example tries to enter a mutex from another thread, first while the main thread holds it, and then after it has left it:
mtx = .ooSQLiteMutex~new mtx~enter say 'While this thread holds it:' tryInAnotherThread(mtx) mtx~leave say 'Once it has left it:' tryInAnotherThread(mtx) mtx~free /* Output: While this thread holds it: busy Once it has left it: entered */
::routine tryInAnotherThread use arg mtx return .message~new(.tryer~new, 'try', 'I', mtx)~~start~result
::class tryer ::method try use arg mtx if mtx~try == .ooSQLite~BUSY then return 'busy' mtx~leave return 'entered'
